description: Survey competition page and existing artifacts to decide what to do next
steps: Step 1: Search for current competition status and rules at https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/kaggle-measuring-agi/overview using web_search
Step 2: Read repo/STATUS.md for current project status
Step 3: Read repo/IAN_TODO.md for pending human action items
Step 4: List all notebooks in repo/notebooks/ and note which tracks are covered (metacognition, learning, attention, exec functions, social cognition)
Step 5: Check repo/results/ — read FRONTIER_MODEL_RESULTS.md and SPOT_TEST_ANALYSIS.md for existing results
Step 6: Check which notebooks are already on Kaggle by reading any upload logs or status trackers in the repo
Step 7: Write a prioritized action plan to sub-workflows/metacognition/SURVEY.md covering: what is done, what is missing, what remaining days should focus on, what agent can do vs what needs Ian

description: Audit metacognition notebooks for kbench SDK compatibility and fix any issues
steps: Step 1: Read the kbench SDK cookbook at repo/research/kaggle_benchmarks_cookbook.md (or search repo for SDK reference docs)

Step 2: For each metacognition notebook (metacog_*.ipynb) in repo/notebooks/, verify: correct @kbench.task() decorator usage, proper return types (bool/float/tuple), valid llm.prompt() calls, dataset loaded via .evaluate() pattern
Step 3: Check that each notebook has exactly one %choose cell at the end selecting the main task
Step 4: List any issues found per notebook in a summary. For each issue, note the cell number and what needs fixing
Step 5: Fix any compatibility issues found directly in the notebook files
Step 6: Write a brief validation report to repo/results/metacog_sdk_audit.md

description: Review and strengthen contamination resistance across all metacognition benchmarks
steps: Step 1: Read repo/notebooks/metacog_canary.ipynb to understand the contamination canary approach

Step 2: For each metacognition benchmark (calibration, control, epistemic_humility, epistemic_revision, error_detection, fok, jol, learning_monitoring), examine the dataset/prompts for memorization vulnerability
Step 3: Check if any benchmark uses well-known trivia, famous examples, or content likely in training data
Step 4: For benchmarks with contamination risk, propose specific modifications: novel stimuli, procedurally generated items, or domain-shifted versions
Step 5: Implement the highest-priority contamination fixes (at least 2 benchmarks)
Step 6: Document changes and rationale in repo/results/contamination_hardening_log.md

description: Analyze spot test results and identify benchmarks that need difficulty calibration
steps: Step 1: Read repo/results/SPOT_TEST_ANALYSIS.md and repo/results/FRONTIER_MODEL_RESULTS.md for existing test data
Step 2: Read any JSON results files in repo/results/ (correlation_analysis.json, mock_validation.json, etc.)
Step 3: Identify benchmarks where models score too high (>90% — ceiling effect) or too low (<10% — floor effect)
Step 4: For ceiling-effect benchmarks, propose specific difficulty increases (harder items, more distractors, stricter scoring)
Step 5: For floor-effect benchmarks, propose simplifications or check if the task is testing the right thing
Step 6: Write analysis and recommendations to repo/results/difficulty_calibration_report.md

description: Improve SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md with stronger cognitive science citations and differentiation from CASK
steps: Step 1: Read repo/SUBMISSION_NARRATIVE.md for the current writeup
Step 2: Read repo/research/competition_landscape.md for CASK and competitor analysis
Step 3: Search web for 3-5 key cognitive science papers on metacognitive monitoring (FOK, JOL, calibration) published 2020-2025
Step 4: Add specific citations and theoretical grounding for each metacognition benchmark in the narrative
Step 5: Strengthen the differentiation section explaining how our benchmarks differ from CASK (which tests 17 models but uses simpler paradigms)
Step 6: Ensure the narrative highlights our unique features: contamination canaries, sub-metric decomposition, procedural generation
